r: If two of your strongest engineers are in conflict and you let it drag on for another quarter of quiet standoffs, the whole team will pay for it. Google's Project Aristotle studied 180 teams and found that psychological safety mattered more than who was on the team. Don't referee personalities; referee interfaces. Most feuds between senior engineers are really disputes over who has design authority, so a clear ownership document naming who decides what usually drains much of the heat. Meet each engineer separately first, and you will likely find that each believes the other is slowing delivery. Then schedule a joint session with a written agenda and one shared, measurable deliverable. Tuckman's 1965 model calls this stage storming, and teams that skip it rarely reach performing. Watch the code review comment threads, because tone shows there before resignations do. If one of them threatens to leave, remember that replacing a senior engineer often costs six to nine months of salary. Mediate early; amputate late.
